[[Euroleague]] | team = Žalgiris Kaunas | number = 55 | nationality = German / American | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1998|5|5|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Eugene, Oregon]] | draft_year = | career_start = 2015 | career_end = | years1 = 2015–2016 | team1 = [[Artland Dragons]] | years2 = 2016–present | team2 = [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] | awards = * [[Karaliaus Mindaugo taurė|King Mindaugas Cup]] champion ([[2017 Karaliaus Mindaugo taurė|2017]]) * [[Lithuanian Basketball League|LKL]] champion ([[2016-17 LKL season|2017]]) }} '''Isaiah Hartenstein''' (born May 5, 1998) is a German-American professional [[basketball]] player who plays for [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] of the [[Lietuvos Krepšinio Lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]].http://www.nbadraft.net/players/isaiah-hartenstein Born in [[Eugene, Oregon]], he is the son of [[Florian Hartenstein]], a German basketball coach and former professional basketball player. Isaiah's mother is American. His parents met in the United States when his father attended the [[University of Oregon]].{{cite web| url = http://www.zeit.de/sport/2015-06/isaiah-hartenstein-basketball-talent | publisher = „Die Zeit“ | title = Großer Mann, was nun? | date = 2015-06-15 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} ==Career== Isaiah started playing basketball in the US, in 2008 he and his family moved to Germany,{{cite web| url = http://www.artland-dragons.de/fileadmin/site/pdf/Drachen-Bote/Drachen-Bote_15-03_April.pdf | publisher = „Artland Dragons“ | title = Isaiah Hartenstein: "Mein Ziel ist die beste Liga der Welt" | date = 2013-03-03 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} where his father was playing professionally. Isaiah joined the [[MTV Gießen]] youth ranks and continued his career at the youth teams of [[QTSV Quakenbrück]]/[[Artland Dragons]], after his father had signed to play with the [[Artland Dragons]] in 2009. In the 2013-14 season, Hartenstein led the Artland Dragons' junior team to a German championship in the 16-under Bundesliga [[JBBL]], while being named Most Valuable Player.{{cite web| url = http://www.nbbl-basketball.de/events/awards-jbbl/ | publisher = „NBBL“ | title = Awards der Jugend Basketball Bundesliga | date = 2016-02-02 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} He averaged 20.9 points, 12.1 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 2.9 steals and 1.9 blocks on the season.{{cite web| url = http://www.nbbl-basketball.de/teams/jbbl/nordwest/#rcd1:/statistik/spieler/index.php%3Fteam_id=2006&saison=2013&spieler_id=21532 | publisher = „NBBL“ | title = Isaiah Hartenstein Steckbrief | date = 2016-02-02 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} His father Florian who served as head coach of the team was named [[JBBL]] Coach of the Year. Hartenstein was selected to play in the 2014 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game: He finished the game with four points and five rebounds in 18 minutes.{{cite web| url = http://jordanbrandclassic.com/wp-content/uploads/archive/2014internationalgameboxscore.pdf | publisher = „Jordan Brand Classic“ | title = Official Basketball Box Score International Black vs International White | date = 2014-04-18 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} On February 1, 2015, he made his debut in Germany's top-tier [[Basketball Bundesliga]], seeing 1:12 minutes of action against [[Eisbären Bremerhaven]].{{cite web| url = http://www.beko-bbl.de/de/n/spielberichte/2014-15/nachbericht/2015-02-01-bre-art/#specialnavi=33 | publisher = „Basketball-Bundesliga“ | title = Boxscore Eisbären Bremerhaven - Artland Dragons | date = 2015-02-01 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} In August 2015, Hartenstein inked a deal with Lithuanian powerhouse [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]], but remained with the Artland Dragons on loan.{{cite web| url = http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/69yd5rpubbe3mwhv/zalgiris-invests-in-top-german-talent-hartenstein | publisher = „Euroleague“ | title = Zalgiris invests in top German talent Hartenstein | date = 2015-08-17 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} The Dragons had withdrawn from the Bundesliga and were relegated to the 2. Bundesliga ProB, Germany's third division. Hartenstein played in 14 games for the [[Quakenbrück]] based side during the 2015–16 campaign, compiling averages of 11.6 points, 8.9 rebounds, 2.1 blocks, 1.6 steals and 1.4 assists.{{cite web| url = http://www.zweite-basketball-bundesliga.de/teams/kader/spieler/2594/ | publisher = „2. Basketball-Bundesliga“ | title = Isaiah Hartenstein | date = 2016-02-02 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} In January 2016, he decided to leave the Artland Dragons to join Žalgiris Kaunas.{{cite web| url = http://www.eurobasket.com/Germany/news/435389/NBA-prospect-Isaiah-Hartenstein-leaves-Quakenbrueck | publisher = „Eurobasket.com“ | title = NBA prospect Isaiah Hartenstein leaves Quakenbrueck | date = 2016-01-22 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} Earlier that month, Hartenstein had helped the Žalgiris Kaunas U18 squad to win the qualifying tournament to the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] and was selected MVP.{{cite web| url = http://www.adidasngt.com/u18/game-center/games/showgame?gamecode=14&seasoncode=JTK15#!report | publisher = „adidasngt.com“ | title = 2015-16 ANGT Kaunas Final | date = 2016-01-17 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} In February 2016, he attended the "Basketball Without Borders Global Camp" during the [[NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Toronto]], [[Canada]].{{Cite web| url = http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Basketball-Without-Borders-Global-Camp-Evaluations-Power-Forwards-5370/| title = DraftExpress: Basketball Without Borders Global Camp Evaluations: Power Forwards| website = www.draftexpress.com| access-date = 2016-02-28}} Hartenstein made his debut for Žalgiris in Lithuania's top-flight [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|LKL]] on September 28, 2016 against Šiauliai{{Cite web|url=http://www.lkl.lt/zaidejas/2382875/|title=Isaiah Hartenstein {{!}} Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|website=Tete-a-Tete Casino-LKL|access-date=2016-10-09}} and in the [[EuroLeague|Euroleague]] against [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahce]] on October 26.{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=23&seasoncode=E2016#!boxscore|title=Fenerbahce Istanbul vs. Zalgiris Kaunas - Game|website=www.euroleague.net|access-date=2016-10-31}} On April 7, 2017, he scored 10 points and grabbed three rebounds in 19:13 minutes of play at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/live-stats/2017/usa-vs-world-select-team-2017.aspx|title=LiveStats - USA vs World Select Team - Nike Hoop Summit|access-date=2017-04-08|language=en-US}} He then declared for the [[2017 NBA Draft]] over two weeks later on April 22. He was also named an invite for the [[2017 NBA Draft|2017]] [[NBA Draft Combine]], but he ultimately declined participation for the event. Later on in the season, he helped Zalgiris win their first ever [[Karaliaus Mindaugo taurė|King Mindaugus Cup]] championship this year. Hartenstein is currently considered a mid-to-late first round pick. By the end of the June 12th NBA Draft deadline, Hartenstein became only one of 10 international draft underclassmen to officially remain in the NBA Draft. ==International career== Hartenstein represented Germany at the 2014 U16{{cite web| url = http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.roundID_9771.season_2014.teamID_288.playerID_108390.html | publisher = „FIBA Europe“ | title = ISAIAH HARTENSTEIN, Germany | date = 2016-01-17 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} and the 2015 U18 European Championships.{{cite web| url = http://u18men.fibaeurope.com/en/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2015.roundID_11484.teamID_288.playerID_108390.html | publisher = „FIBA Europe“ | title = U18 European Championship Men, ISAIAH HARTENSTEIN, Germany | date = 2016-02-02 | accessdate = 2016-02-02}} In December 2016, he helped carry Germany to a fourth-place finish at the U18 European Championships, averaging team-highs 14.7 points, 9.5 rebounds, 1.7 blocks and 1.7 steals a contest,{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/europe/u18/2016/Germany|title=Germany at the FIBA U18 European Championship Division A 2016 - FIBA.com|website=FIBA.com|access-date=2016-12-22}} which earned him a spot in the tournament's "All-Star Five".{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/europe/u18/2016/news/france-crowned-champions-at-fiba-u18-european-championship|title=France crowned champions at FIBA U18 European Championship|website=FIBA.com|access-date=2016-12-22}} ==Career stats== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===ProB=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| 2015–16 | style="text-align:left;"| [[QTSV Quakenbrück]] | 14 || 10 || 24.4 || .479 || .425 || .544 || 8.9 || 1.3 || 1.6 || 2.1 || 11.5 {{S-end}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{BC Žalgiris current roster}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Hartenstein, Isaiah}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Artland Dragons players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Oregon]] [[Category:BC Žalgiris players]] [[Category:German men's basketball players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Eugene, Oregon]]
